title: Assemble the Payment Run
scenario: It is 2:45 PM. Fifteen minutes to the cutoff, and here is the payoff of the whole desk: every value the payment run needs already lives in an artifact you built. Fill each slot by LOOKING IT UP on the shelf - the batch, the vendor master, the approval. If you catch yourself recalculating a total, stop: the pipeline already did it.
input: Assembly rule: every slot value must come from a stored artifact. The invoice count and run total are in payment-batch.json. The pay-to name, vendor id, and bank on file are in the vendor master. The approver and approval time are in run-approval.json. The run date is day-1; funds are delivered to the Payables DL at the 3:00 PM cutoff.
instructions: Open each artifact on the shelf as you need it - do not work from memory.
Fill the header slots from the run approval (approver, time, cutoff).
Fill the batch slots from the payment batch (count, total).
Fill the pay-to slots from the vendor master (name, id, bank).

copilotPrompt: Assemble a payment run by looking up values in stored artifacts: count and total from the payment batch, approver and time from the run approval, and pay-to name, vendor id, and bank from the vendor master. Do not recompute the total.
successMessage: Payment run rendered. Every value traces to an artifact - the run assembled in minutes because the pipeline did the work.

sections.title: The highest fan-in on the desk
sections.body: The payment run pulls from more artifacts than anything else - which is why it is nearly last. Assembly is cheap only because the batch, the vendor master, and the approval already exist as trusted objects.

sections.title: Never recompute the total
sections.body: The run total is in the payment batch. If assembly re-added the invoices and rounded differently, the run and the batch would disagree - two sources of truth. Assembly reads; it does not derive.

sections.title: Bank details come from the master
sections.body: The pay-to name and bank are read from the governed vendor master, never from the invoice. That single rule is the fraud control that stops payment redirection at the last step.

sections.title: Traceability is the quality bar
sections.body: The run is release-ready when every value traces to an artifact: totals to the batch, approver to the approval, bank to the master. That property, not formatting, is what makes it trustworthy.

takeaway.heading: Payment run assembled
points: You produced the day's payment run without deriving a single value - every slot was a lookup into an artifact you built.
The run is fully traceable: totals to the batch, approver to the run approval, pay-to details to the vendor master.
The bank on file came from the governed master, never the invoice - the last-step fraud control.
payment-run.md is stored as a rendered document, delivered to the Payables DL at the cutoff.
The workflow can now assemble a release-ready payment run entirely from upstream artifacts.
